A twelve-scenario harness (no bridge, no city module, inert city, ready() throws, an older bundle with only budget(), catalog entry gone, placed() throws, placed() returns a non-array, effect() throws, malformed rows, no origin node, junk garageTier) produced a typed value from every export in every state and never threw. That verification discipline sits above this repo's bar. What holds the round back is one false safety claim, and it is on the paid rail.

That argument is about nodes; the divergence is about a cap number. Nothing stops two freightdepot rows sitting in that one placed array: build() (production.state.js:424) checks prereqs and cost and then pushes, with no uniqueness test, and city/index.js:138 wires a build button per catalog entry. Two L1 yards therefore make sumFleetCap() report 8 while transport_caps() computes least(4 * depot_level, max_fleet_rigs) = 4 off ONE depot_level, and trg_ins (sql/038:813) refuses the fifth registration when fleet_slots_left hits 0 — a rig bought on the PP floor that will not register. The sum is the brief's pinned contract and should stay — what must change is the claim, from 'unreachable' to 'reachable by placing a second yard, and here is what the player is shown', with the header no longer naming fleetCap() as an agree-with-the-server case. ab_reasoning: A is production.state.js; B is production.data.js. Both are far above ordinary code and the call was close. A wins because every comment in it is pinned to the branch it justifies and carries a measured consequence in the units the player lost: 'a collect promised 810 food and banked 540: 270 units destroyed, clipped:false, and the 36h timer reset. Measured, not theorised'; the refund-on-record-failure path documented as having been DEAD CODE because the adapter swallowed the throw, with the driven result ('{ok:true} and charged 50,000 Cinder + 80 metal for a building that was never persisted') and the fix landed on both sides of the seam; cityBudget's crew-scaling change flagged as a real balance change with the level-3 Foundry numbers and 'Reported to the coordinator'. It declares authority where doing so costs it something ('THE CAP REPORTED HERE IS THE LEDGER'S OWN CAP, NOT A LOCAL BELIEF'), refuses to redeclare the 6h/36h idle contract so production cannot become a third policy, and marks its unimplemented hook honestly ('cityOutputMultipliers() DOES NOT EXIST... I grepped the whole of index.html'). B is genuinely excellent — the rejected merge into CAMP_FACILITIES costed in read sites, the CITY_PREREQ cycle argument, and an auditCatalog() that makes the acceptance criteria runnable instead of prose are all top of this repo's range, and the freightdepot block's rejected 'inputs: { fuel: 30 }' is argued in three ordered, checkable facts. What puts it second is proportion and provenance: roughly a hundred lines of commentary sit on a fifteen-line data literal, much of it exposition about another file's SQL rather than about the literal it guards, and one paragraph exists to correct a claim the same block made wrongly a round earlier. Honest, but it spends its authority on cross-references, where A spends its on branches that prevent measured losses.
builder_response:
The gap was real and I reproduced it before fixing it: with window.MythicCityProduction registered and MythicCityBridge absent, host() is null, MP.placed() returns [], and depotReady() printed code 'no-depot' with fix "Build a Freight Depot in your city" for a save holding one. Checks 1 and 2 could not catch it because the transport bridge is fine and cityProdDef() resolves off a static import that never needed a host.

Fix: a `city-inert` branch ahead of the no-depot branch, using the discriminator the critic named — `ready: () => !!makeHost()` at city/index.js:106 — with `budget() !== null` (index.js:115) as an older-bundle fallback and a throwing ready() counted as not-live. Its `fix` string contains nothing a player can act on by building anything, and names the console line the city module has already printed.

Driving that fix surfaced two more routes to the identical wrong sentence, both now closed: a live city whose catalog entry is missing (`catalog-missing`, ordered after inert because only the live case is pruning the save), and a placed() that throws (`rows-unreadable`, closed at source by placedRows() returning {ok, rows}). Four of the eight checks now exist solely to keep that sentence off the screen, and the check-order note says so.

The two false cross-file claims are corrected rather than annotated: (a) sql/038 does NOT compute reach in transport_quote and bays in transport_dispatch as literals — that is the migration's rejected first draft, and the live authority is transport_caps() at sql/038:628; (b) fleetCap()'s claim that the server never checks fleet size is false, trg_ins at sql/038:813 enforces it via fleet_slots_left, with the migration's measured 60-rigs-into-a-cap-4-charter incident quoted. Both corrections are labelled as corrections, with the wrong version stated, so the next reader is not sent back to it. The same false claim in production.data.js was fixed in the same edit.
